No-go theorems for sublinear-depth group designs

pH-responsive Keto-Enol tautomerism in a β-ketoenamine covalent organic framework for selective thorium(IV) capture
HuBMAP Data Portal: a resource for multimodal spatial and single-cell data of healthy human tissues
articles.abstract: Abstract The NIH Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP) Data Portal ( https://portal.hubmapconsortium.org/ ) serves as a comprehensive repository for multimodal, multi-scale spatial and single-cell data from healthy human tissues. As of August 2026, the portal hosts 9,316 public datasets from 26 data types spanning 29 organ classes across 501 donors. Portal infrastructure and user interfaces support data search and discovery, visualization, and analysis directly in web browsers. These capabilities include metadata- and data-driven search, collaborative Workspaces with access to high-performance compute, and interactive Vitessce visualizations across non-spatial, 2D, and 3D spatial datasets. Data-type-specific uniform processing pipelines and rigorous quality control processes ensure comparability of results across laboratories, organs, and donors, while externally processed community-contributed datasets provide complementary perspectives. Here we describe portal functionality, infrastructure, and design, and highlight its role as a platform for large-scale spatial single-cell research across diverse data types, organs, and scales.

articles.title: PrinTE: a forward simulation framework for studying the role of transposable elements in genome expansion and contraction
articles.abstract: Abstract Genome expansion and contraction are driven by transposable element activity, but the underlying dynamics remain enigmatic due to a lack of historical records tracing these changes. Here, we present PrinTE, a forward-time simulator of whole-genome sequences with customizable transposon dynamics for identifying the evolutionary parameters most consistent with an observed genome. Across simulations spanning four orders of magnitude, PrinTE recovers transposon insertion and deletion rates with less than 6% error. We demonstrate PrinTE on Arabidopsis and the fungal subdivision Pucciniomycotina, including myrtle rust ( Austropuccinia psidii ), which expanded its genome size to 1,018 Mb through transposon amplifications. Our simulations show that recombination-based removal of LTR retrotransposons alone cannot prevent genome obesity, and that preventing their invasion in the first place is more effective. We hypothesize that A. psidii might have experienced a prolonged expansion phase followed by a potent and ongoing period of contraction.

articles.title: Short-depth designs beyond the unitary group
A distinct class of conjugative megaplasmids is associated with prophages in distantly related bacterial lineages
Evidence of widespread sequencing errors in global avian influenza study
Ketogenic diet stimulates tumor cGAS-Sting pathway and attenuates systemic inflammation via Flavonifractor plautii derived uridine
Microglia-dependent PDGFB regulation of neuronal KCND2 in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus determines propofol anesthesia induction
articles.abstract: Abstract Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying anesthetic-induced unconsciousness remains a central question in both anesthesia research and neuroscience. However, the role of non-neuronal components in modulating anesthetic sensitivity is poorly understood. In this study, we identify a microglia-dependent platelet-derived growth factor subunit B (PDGFB) signaling pathway that modulates propofol anesthesia sensitivity and contributes to the induction of anesthesia in mice. We demonstrate that PDGFB signaling regulates the potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 2 (KCND2) in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) in mice, thereby orchestrating the excitability of PVN glutamatergic neurons (PVN Glu ) and the activity of their projections to lateral hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons (LH Glu ). Microglia deprivation induces PDGFB deficiency and downregulates KCND2, resulting in PVN hyperexcitability and hyperactivation of the PVN → LH arousal circuit, which contributes to resistance to anesthesia induction in mice. Our findings identified non-neuronal molecular mechanism that governs anesthetic sensitivity, complementing the classical γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor-centric model and providing insights into the regulation of anesthesia induction.

articles.title: The Genome Atlas of 1,020 Probands and 409 Unaffected Parents Decodes the Clinical Heterogeneity in β-thalassemia
Complex magnetism in a transition metal nitride
articles.abstract: Abstract High-symmetry lattices of transition metal ions such as the body-centred tetragonal (bct) arrangement are model systems for correlated electron physics and frustrated magnetism. Transition metal oxides or halides with the bct K 2 NiF 4 -type structure are extensively studied and have ground states dominated by strong interactions within the square layers, but materials exemplifying other bct ground states are much rarer. Here we show that Ca 2 CoN 2 , from the underexplored class of transition metal nitrides, has one of the complex magnetic ground states predicted for the bct lattice lying close to a spin-liquid instability. Ca 2 CoN 2 has been synthesised at high pressure in a large-volume press, and has a Na 2 HgO 2 -type structure where weakening of intralayer superexchange interactions leads to frustration. Our magnetisation and neutron diffraction experiments reveal an incommensurate spin order below 54 K, consistent with a double- k spin density wave with propagation vectors ( k 00) and (0 k 0) where k = 0.57. This phase lies close to the predicted crossover (at k = 0.64–0.69) to a modulated spin liquid, which could be explored through further chemical tuning. This work demonstrates the potential of transition metal nitrides as magnetic model systems, alongside the much-studied oxides and halides, for exploring complex spin orders and associated quantum phases.

articles.title: Algal symbiosis adaptively restructures the cnidarian microbiome to enhance holobiont metabolism
articles.abstract: Abstract Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. Here, we show that symbiosis with photosynthetic dinoflagellates induces adaptive, tissue-specific restructuring of the microbiome in the cnidarian model Aiptasia, fundamentally enhancing holobiont nitrogen assimilation and metabolic flexibility. Using laser microdissection, tissue-resolved metatranscriptomics, gnotobiotic hosts, and stable isotope tracing, we reveal that symbiosis profoundly restructures microbial communities across the epidermis and gastrodermis, enriching for taxa and pathways that support nitrogen assimilation in photosynthetically active tissues. Expression of microbial nitrite reductase is strongly upregulated in the symbiotic gastrodermis, and 15 N-tracer experiments demonstrate that bacterial assimilation of nitrite synergizes with algal symbionts to fuel the biosynthesis of essential amino acids. These findings show that symbiosis drives spatially compartmentalized microbiome adaptation within animal tissues, aligning microbial metabolism with host-algal nutrient exchanges to enhance holobiont functioning.

articles.title: TH-positive pulmonary nerve fiber-epithelial interaction promotes adipose thermogenesis in male mice
An NLR protein with two distinct LRR domains mediates resistance to wheat powdery mildew
articles.abstract: Abstract Powdery mildew is a devastating fungal disease of wheat. Aegilops caudata , a wild relative of common wheat, is highly resistant to powdery mildew. However, the presence of chromosomal structural variations and the absence of a reference genome for Ae. caudata have significantly hindered the cloning and breeding application of resistance genes from this species. Here, we report the cloning of powdery mildew resistance gene Pm7C from Ae. caudata by integrating map-based cloning, collinearity and Pm7C -direct donor transcriptome analysis. Pm7C encodes a nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) protein containing two distinct LRR domains. The resistance function of Pm7C is validated by mutagenesis, gene silencing and transgenic assay. The coiled coil (CC) domain of Pm7C induces cell death and self-associates. Additionally, we develop a set of Pm7C introgression lines and a Pm7C- specific diagnostic molecular marker. Cloning of Pm7C will shed light on NLR protein-mediated disease resistance and accelerate its deployment in wheat breeding.

articles.title: MELK drives neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis via vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic transition
articles.abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular diseases associated with atherosclerosis and post-injury restenosis remain leading global causes of mortality. Despite therapeutic advancements, effective treatments targeting the phenotypic transition of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs)—a pivotal event in neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis—are still limited. This study identifies Maternal Embryonic Leucine Zipper Kinase (MELK) as a key regulator of VSMC phenotypic transition in both injury-induced neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis. MELK is significantly upregulated in VSMCs in response to pathological stimuli, driven by transcriptional activation through C/EBPβ. Mechanistically, MELK phosphorylates EZH2 at threonine 367, stabilizing it and enhancing H3K27me3 modifications on VSMC contractile genes, thereby promoting VSMC dedifferentiation. SMC-specific knockout of MELK substantially reduces neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis in mouse models. Notably, selective MELK inhibitor OTSSP167 significantly diminishes neointimal hyperplasia without impairing re-endothelialization, a critical process for vascular repair. This study highlights the potential of MELK inhibition as an approach to treating restenosis and atherosclerosis.

Hydrophilic Nanoisland
Interface Engineering for Conquering
Activity–Stability Trade-Off in High-Efficiency Salt Lake Lithium
Extraction
articles.abstract: Abstract The adsorption-based lithium extraction technology from ultralow-grade salt lake brine is severely restricted by the inherent activity–stability trade-off of traditional granular Li/Al-LDHs adsorbents (GLDHs). Herein, a nanoisland encapsulation strategy integrated with hydrophilic interface engineering is developed to fabricate Li/Al-LDHs composite granules with tailored hydrophilic interfaces (HILDHs), breaking the long-standing bottleneck of conventional aluminum-based lithium adsorbents used in the salt lake industry. Systematic experiments and multiscale simulations reveal that the strong water affinity of polyacrylonitrile cyano groups (−C≡N) creates a highly hydrated microenvironment for rapid Li+ transport, while the nanoisland-confined structure anchors Li/Al-LDHs nanosheets to preserve the layered framework under harsh deep desorption conditions, thus enabling excellent cycling stability. The optimized HILDHs deliver a 3.02-fold higher working adsorption capacity (7.25 mg g–1 vs 2.40 mg g–1 for GLDHs) in actual Qarhan old brine within 60 min, along with a 13.36-fold increase in adsorption rate constant, 40% lower rinsing water consumption, and excellent cycle stability. It is calculated the nanoisland encapsulation strategy can achieve a nearly 5-fold increase for the annual Li2CO3 production capacity from salt lake lithium industrial lines.

articles.title:
Modeling Decadal
Organosulfates in Particulate Matter
to Improve Estimations of Aerosol Hygroscopicity in the United States
articles.abstract: Abstract Organosulfates (OSs) can comprise a substantial fraction of secondary organic aerosol and exhibit significantly different hygroscopicity than inorganic sulfates, yet their spatiotemporal prevalence and climatic impacts remain poorly constrained because speciated measurements are sparse and common chemical transport models do not explicitly represent OS formation. This study develops a flexible and robust modeling framework to quantify isoprene-derived OS (iOS) concentrations and OS impacts on aerosol hygroscopicity (κ) across the contiguous United States (U.S.) for summers spanning 2013–2022. Using the Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model with updated iOS chemistry, simulations reproduce Interagency Monitoring of Protected Visual Environments (IMPROVE) network-derived organosulfur and inorganic sulfate and agree with speciated iOS measurements from filter analyses. OS concentrations are elevated in the eastern U.S., with summertime mean values up to 0.51 μg m–3. OS formation produces a net 5.6% decrease in κ (direct OS contribution, +2.8%; indirect, −8.4% via sulfate reduction). We apply an interpretable machine-learning surrogate to identify predictive features associated with OS variability and enable efficient estimation without rerunning CMAQ. These results provide the first observation-validated, high-spatial-coverage OS reconstruction and nationwide quantification of OS-driven κ changes, underscoring the importance of representing OS formation and expanded observations to improve aerosol-cloud radiative effect assessments.

articles.title:
Context-Aware
Multitask Learning for Aquatic and Soil
Ecotoxicity Prediction from Fragmented ECOTOX Records
articles.abstract: Abstract Large ecotoxicity databases contain extensive evidence, yet heterogeneous reporting and sparse coverage across chemicals, species, end points, and conditions limit predictive use. From relational U.S. EPA ECOTOX, we linked 1,234,077 traceable records and constructed model-ready aquatic and soil data sets of 219,818 and 11,532 records. We developed a context-aware multitask model that preserves end point-specific responses while sharing information across molecular, biological, and experimental contexts. On held-out condition keys and parent-species-task combinations, four-seed ensembles achieved pooled R2 of 0.758/0.751 for aquatic toxicity and 0.628/0.537 for soil toxicity. Compared with same-input single-task models, multitask fitting reduced soil task-macro mean absolute error (MAE) by 0.136/0.156 across 16 task heads; aquatic point estimates also favored sharing, although uncertainty across all aquatic task heads was not estimable. Under canonical-parent holdout, frozen shared representations reduced task-macro MAE by 0.170–0.180 in aquatic and 0.093–0.125 in soil tree models versus molecular-only inputs, indicating reusable predictive information. Multidimensional training support stratified parent-holdout errors, meeting prespecified criteria fully for soil and partially for aquatic predictions; benefits weakened under stronger structural separation. These results show model-ready ECOTOX data can support context-aware toxicity prediction across a sparse experimental matrix, helping prioritize informative measurements and providing a predictive evidence base for environmental hazard assessment.

articles.title:
Coupled
Geophysical
and Technoeconomic Industrial
Growth Constraints on Geological Carbon Storage Scale-Up: Application
to UK Offshore Resources
articles.abstract: Abstract Geological carbon dioxide storage is central to meeting many national climate change commitments, but large-scale deployment may be limited by both techno-economic rates of growth and physics-based processes imposed by subsurface geology. We develop a modeling framework for the assessment of feasible CO2 storage scale-up trajectories that unifies constraints arising from industrial rates of growth, dynamic injection rate limits from reservoir pressurization, and static maximum cumulative storage resource. We employ logistic and Gompertz models to represent policy-compliant deployment trajectories, parametrized by the total cumulative storage resource. We then use a simplified physics model to estimate the resulting regional subsurface pressurization along these trajectories. Growth curves where reservoir pressurization exceeds safe limits are updated by reducing the static storage resource until residing in the safe deployment range. The result is both a growth trajectory and static storage resource achievable subject to injectivity limits. Applying the framework to the United Kingdom (UK), we find that offshore storage resources are sufficient to accommodate all government midcentury deployment rate scenarios up to 175 Mt yr–1. Cumulative storage of up to 78 Gt, representing a reference estimate of the UK storage resource base used in national planning, can be achieved under Gompertz growth trajectories. The more aggressive logistic trajectories are constrained by reservoir pressure, limiting the achievable resource base to 69 Gt. The framework is transferable to other regions to assess the feasibility of policy-driven CO2 storage pathways under coupled industrial growth and geophysical constraints, informing national decarbonization planning and global integrated assessment models.

articles.title:
Molecular Insights
into a Precursor–Chlorine
Trade-Off Governing Divergent Formation Pathways of PCDD/Fs and Emerging
Cl-PAHs in Waste Cocombustion of Cellulose, PET, and PVC
articles.abstract: Abstract Co-combustion of industrial and municipal solid waste (ISW/MSW) is widely practiced, yet PCDD/Fs and emerging chlorinated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (Cl-PAHs) formation under mixed-feedstock conditions remains poorly understood. Here, cellulose, polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) were combusted individually and cocombusted with MSW to elucidate how feedstock chemistry regulates chlorinated pollutant formation. Comprehensive mass-spectrometric profiling of target pollutants, aromatic precursors, and the top 50 combustion intermediates, combined with DFT calculations, revealed a precursor–chlorine trade-off governing pollutant formation. PET preferentially generated oxygenated aromatic intermediates, particularly dibenzofuran; PVC supplied the most PAHs and reactive chlorine, and cellulose primarily contributed carbon skeletons. Accordingly, two distinct pathways were proposed: dibenzofuran-centered, chlorination-limited formation of PCDD/Fs and stepwise aromatic growth followed by site-selective chlorination of Cl-PAHs. The higher HOMO energies of two representative PAHs, anthracene and phenanthrene, relative to dibenzofuran indicated their greater susceptibility to electrophilic chlorination. Consequently, Cl-PAHs exceeded PCDD/Fs by 1–3 orders of magnitude and accounted for 83.4% of estimated TEQ. Increasing chlorine availability alleviated the kinetic constraint on dibenzofuran chlorination, causing an approximately 42-fold increase in PCDD/F emissions at 20% PVC blending. These findings establish a molecular basis for feedstock-chemistry-guided management and broaden emission-control priorities from regulated PCDD/Fs to emerging Cl-PAHs.

articles.title:
Polyethylene Terephthalate
Oligomers in Disposable
Diapers: Occurrence, Dermal Exposure and Health Assessment
articles.abstract: Abstract Disposable infant diapers commonly use multicomponent nonwoven fabrics containing polyethylene terephthalate (PET), from which PET oligomer byproducts may be released and transferred to infant skin. In this study, 6 cyclic PET oligomers (C[TPA+EG]2–7) were detected in the top sheets and absorbent cores of 37 disposable diapers. ∑C[TPA+EG]2–7 averaged 198 ± 98.7 μg/g (top sheets) and 66.6 ± 49.2 μg/g (absorbent cores), dominated by C[TPA+EG]3 (95.9% and 92.3%). Oligomer levels positively correlated with diaper PET content, confirming an in situ polymer source. During a 3-day in-use study, 1348–2318 ng of oligomers migrated to infant buttock skin and remained partially after water washing, corresponding to an estimated C[TPA+EG]3 exposure of 8.80–182 ng/kg BW/day. Network toxicology and molecular docking identified potential targets and pathways associated with local skin effects, including inflammation, barrier regulation, apoptosis, and extracellular matrix remodeling, suggesting potential local skin-health implications. Our results establish diaper dermal contact as a critical infant plastic oligomer exposure route and raise health concerns for vulnerable infant skin.

articles.title:
Fingerprints of
Airborne Plastics in Urban PM2.5: Applications and Implications
articles.abstract: Abstract To better identify emission sources of airborne plastics, we employed nine plastic-associated chemicals (PlsACs) in 240 daily PM2.5 samples collected in Singapore during 2018–2020. A unique PlsAC, tris(2,4-ditert-butylphenyl) phosphate (I168O), is most abundant, accounting for 90% of the total quantified PlsACs and identifying at least 40% more PM2.5 linked to respirable airborne PlsACs. A newly resolved source of plastic production, use, and burning (PlasticPub) accounts for the highest fraction (37%) of the quantified PlsACs among the seven apportioned PM2.5 sources. Nearly all di-iso-butyl phthalate (DIBP) and more than half of di-n-butyl phthalate (DNBP) are attributed to two factors of Background and Marine aerosols, indicating their potential worldwide transport. More than 90% of diethyl phthalate (DEP) is associated with transported peat forest (PF) burning smoke, demonstrating involvement of anthropogenic activities. Following PlasticPub, Traffic & road dust is the second predominant source responsible for >20% of the near-range PlsACs and featured with a DNBP/di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate (DEHP) concentration ratio of 2.2. The DNBP/DEHP concentration ratio higher than 1 can indicate nonexhaust emissions from on-road traffic due to abrasion of tires, brakes, and road markings. The average enrichment ratio of quantified PlsACs within PM2.5 (ng PlsACs per μg PM2.5) for each resolved source provides a basis for assessing strategies to cocontrol airborne plastics and PM2.5.

articles.title:
Atmospheric Aging
Modifies the Toxicological Profile
of Biomass Burning Particles in Epithelial Lung Cells
articles.abstract: Abstract Wildfire activity and associated smoke emissions are increasing globally, leading to widespread exposure to biomass burning particulate matter (PM). Although people are mainly exposed to aged wildfire smoke rather than fresh emissions, the effects of atmospheric aging on wildfire particulate toxicity remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how atmospheric processing (“aging”) modifies biological effects of biomass burning particles (BBPs) generated under controlled flaming and smoldering combustion conditions. BB emissions were produced in the Photochemical Large Aerosol Chamber (PHOTO-LAC) and aged under alternating photochemical and dark conditions. Fresh and aged BBP extracts were subsequently sampled and tested in human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B). We assessed cytotoxicity, oxidative stress, oxidative DNA damage, genome-wide transcriptional responses, and inflammatory and extracellular matrix-related protein expression. Atmospheric aging substantially altered BBP toxicity in a combustion-dependent manner. Aged BBP enhanced intracellular reactive oxygen species formation and oxidative DNA damage, particularly for smoldering emissions, while cytotoxicity remained largely unchanged. In contrast, inflammatory and matrix-remodeling responses were attenuated with aging in smoldering particles but remained stable for flaming BBP. These findings demonstrate that atmospheric aging can simultaneously amplify oxidative and genotoxic stress while dampening inflammatory signaling, underscoring the need to incorporate aging state into health risk assessments of wildfire smoke exposure.

articles.title:
Free-Radical Cascade
Mediates Humus Formation in Mineral-Rich
Organic Matrices
articles.abstract: Abstract Humus formation in nature is traditionally viewed as a lengthy microbial enzymatic process, yet the abiotic pathways remain unclear. Here, by employing iron-mineral-rich composting as a model system that amplifies and accelerates natural humification, we reveal a free-radical cascade that drives abiotic humification. Magnetite addition amplified hydroxyl radical (•OH) production 1.5-fold (1289.4 μmol·kg–1) and enriched humus precursors (amino acids, polyphenols, reducing sugars), ultimately yielding 1.5 times more humic acid (135.6 mg/g) with higher molecular weight and stronger aromatic condensation. Mass spectrometry combined with density functional theory calculations identified multiple environmentally persistent free radicals (EPFRs), including semiquinone and phenoxy radicals as key intermediates that couple precursors into macromolecular humus. Simulated transformation experiments with selective microbial inactivation and •OH scavenging demonstrated that the abiotic radical pathway contributed approximately 33.4% to humus formation. We propose a free-radical cascade: •OH-driven oxidative fragmentation of organic matter followed by EPFR-mediated humus precursors coupling. These findings establish an unrecognized abiotic dimension of humification, reshaping our mechanistic understanding of organic carbon stabilization and offering nature-based strategies for soil carbon sequestration and remediation in organic-mineral interaction environments.

articles.title:
Calibration of Passive
Sampling Eyewear to Assess
Inhalation Exposure
articles.abstract: Abstract Calibrated wearable passive air samplers are critical tools for accessibly quantifying individualized and population exposures to airborne pollution, a leading cause of chronic disease. Our lab recently introduced passive sampling eyewear (PSE) to address gaps in tools tailored for measuring and mitigating risks from inhalation exposure. The PSE, like most existing designs of wearable samplers, is largely uncalibrated. An exception is the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) brooch, and mini-polyurethane foam (PUF) samplers, which have been calibrated for only 27 compounds. Here, we calibrate PSE against active air samplers codeployed in both stationary and wearable forms in office and home environments to capture a wide range of exposure scenarios. We report sampling rates (RS) and inhalation exposure for over 200 features covering diverse physical-chemical properties measured using the Orbitrap gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (GC–MS) system in both targeted and nontargeted modes. RS were 0.70 ± 0.62 m3 day–1 dm–2 for stationary and 0.85 ± 0.68 m3 day–1 dm–2 for wearable deployments, with no significant difference (p = 0.06) between the deployment types. Wearable calibration captured higher RS and variability, as expected for personal sampling, because participants’ movement and daily activity can alter airflow and disrupt the stagnant air-boundary layer around the sampler. In terms of analysis mode, RS derived from targeted and nontargeted analysis (NTA) were reasonably comparable for a given compound, differing by ∼1.5-fold, boosting confidence in using NTA approaches for expanding databases of RS. Applying the wearable RS, the profiles and levels of inhalation exposure varied widely between participants when at home versus in offices, reflecting differences in exposure sources and dynamics between the two environments. Overall, the findings from both the calibration and field studies represent a significant step toward quantitatively assessing inhalation exposure using PSE.

Liquid
Crystal Monomers
in Paired Indoor Dust and
Urine: Compound-Specific Enrichment Patterns and External–Internal
Exposure Profiles
articles.abstract: Abstract Liquid crystal monomers (LCMs) are extensively used in liquid crystal display devices, yet the relationship between household contamination and human internal exposure remains unclear. We investigated fluorinated and nonfluorinated LCMs (FLCMs and NFLCMs) in paired indoor dust and urine samples. Widespread occurrence of LCMs was observed in 58 paired indoor dust and first-morning urine samples collected in Suizhou, with 48 of 49 LCMs detected in dust and 40 in urine. Median concentrations of ∑49LCMs were 255 ng/g in dust and 26.9 ng/mL in urine. FLCMs were predominant in dust, whereas NFLCMs contributed more to urinary burden. The dominant compounds differed markedly between dust and urine. Among these, only 2,3-difluoro-1-methoxy-4-[4-(4-propylcyclohexyl)cyclohexyl]benzene (DMPCB) showed a significant positive dust-urine correlation (r = 0.409, p < 0.01). Relative-enrichment analysis revealed compound-specific shifts, with several NFLCMs relatively enriched in urine and several FLCMs in dust. The median estimated daily intake of ∑49LCMs via dust ingestion was 0.110 ng/kg bw/day, far below levels reported for e-waste recycling areas. Although hazard quotients (HQs) for all 39 LCMs with available toxicity benchmarks were several orders of magnitude below 1, incomplete toxicity reference data remain a major source of uncertainty in risk characterization. Overall, the findings indicate widespread mixed exposure to LCMs and suggest that urinary LCM profiles may reflect contributions from multiple exposure pathways and compound-specific toxicokinetic processes in addition to household dust.

articles.title:
Stage-Resolved Dynamics
of Antibiotic Resistance Genes
and Mobile Genetic Elements in Full-Scale Anaerobic Digestion Systems
articles.abstract: Abstract Anaerobic digestion (AD) has the potential to reduce antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) during waste treatment, yet evidence from full-scale systems remains limited. In particular, process-stage dynamics and host-associated resistance mechanisms are poorly understood, and the relative importance of operational and physicochemical drivers remains unresolved. Here, we profiled process-oriented, stage-resolved resistome and mobilome dynamics across substrates, digestates, and storages from ten farm-scale AD plants, resolving putative host-ARG-MGE coabundance associations across sequential process stages. An integrated framework combining high-throughput qPCR and 16S rRNA gene sequencing was used to quantify ARG and MGE dynamics and characterize microbial community structure. Across different AD systems, ARGs and MGEs exhibited heterogeneous abundance changes, with no consistent patterns. However, elevated pH and NH3 were associated with decreasing trends but were not solely determinative. Stage-resolved correlation networks revealed that ARG-MGE associations formed a conserved structural backbone, whereas putative host associations underwent continuous reshuffling across process stages. This indicates that resistance persistence is driven less by stable taxon associations and more by the redistribution of ARG-MGE units among microbial taxa. Collectively, these results demonstrate that stage-resolved, network-informed analyses provide an informative framework for evaluating resistance persistence and potential environmental risks associated with digestate application.

articles.title:
Intensifying Mainstream
Wastewater Treatment via a
Dual-Hydrogel Process Coupling Acidic Partial Nitritation and Anammox
articles.abstract: Abstract Partial nitritation and anammox (PN/A) process has been proposed as a sustainable biotechnology for mainstream nitrogen removal. However, it remains challenging to sustain high activities of ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB) and anammox bacteria and suppress the growth of nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB). In this study, a novel dual-hydrogel system comprising two reactors with distinct immobilized microbial communities was developed to integrate acidic PN and anammox for low-strength mainstream wastewater treatment. The system achieved a total inorganic nitrogen removal efficiency of 81.7% at a short overall hydraulic retention time of 5.5 h. In the acidic PN reactor, hydrogel beads effectively immobilized and enriched acid-tolerant AOB (“Candidatus Nitrosoglobus”), while creating a localized low-pH niche with sufficient free nitrous acid microenvironment to selectively inhibit NOB growth. This enabled high-rate PN without strict dissolved oxygen limitation. A pH-based feeding strategy allowed the bulk pH of the acidic PN reactor to be self-maintained at ∼6.1, achieving an appropriate effluent ratio of nitrite to ammonium and minimizing acid inhibition of the downstream anammox process. In the anammox reactor, the beads maintained a relatively higher internal pH, forming a favorable niche for retained anammox bacteria (“Candidatus Brocadia”) and facilitating high-rate nitrogen removal. The hydrogel beads also exhibited excellent structural stability during long-term operation (over 300 days). These results demonstrate an effective approach for simultaneously sustaining AOB and anammox activities while suppressing NOB, providing a promising approach for stable PN/A to treat mainstream wastewater.

articles.title:
In
Situ Reconstruction-Directed
Electrocatalyst Design
Enables Low-Energy Anodic Oxidation for Water Purification
articles.abstract: Abstract Anodic oxidation reactions (AORs) hold promise for degrading persistent organic pollutants, yet practical deployment is constrained by inadequate anode stability and sluggish kinetics under low-bias operation. Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) feature cyanide-bridged metal frameworks with efficient intermetallic electron transfer, yet their surfaces inevitably undergo uncontrolled reconstruction during electrolysis, producing outcomes that range from beneficial activation to detrimental degradation. Here, we reported a first-ever paradigm shift from suppressing reconstruction to actively directing it, demonstrating that the intrinsic instability of FeMn PBA could be harnessed as a design lever. Through an in situ self-reconstruction process, we discovered that the morphology and surface coordination environment were spontaneously reorganized into FeMn nanoflowers grown on carbon paper (FeMn@CP), a configuration never before achieved from this precursor. This reconstruction-guided pathway uniquely yielded a 201-fold increase in electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) over pristine FeMn PBA, alongside markedly enhanced electrochemical stability, synergistic gains not attainable by conventional stabilization strategies. Capitalizing on this reconstructed architecture, FeMn@CP achieved efficient phenolic pollutant degradation at low bias, with robust reusability, broad matrix adaptability, and substantially reduced effluent toxicity. Continuous-flow experiments further verified its sustained performance under practical conditions. This study unveils, for the first time, that catalyst reconstruction, when rationally exploited, serves as a decisive and generalizable strategy to concurrently boost AOR activity and stability, opening an unexplored avenue for designing next-generation electrocatalytic water purification systems.

articles.title:
Fog
Intensity and Droplet Size-Resolved Aqueous Secondary
Organic Aerosol (aqSOA) Formation in Polluted Winter Fog: New Insights
from a Combined Observational and Modeling Study
articles.abstract: Abstract Fog is a chemically active aqueous medium in which dissolved organic gases and particles are converted into highly oxidized aqueous secondary organic aerosol (aqSOA). Its magnitude is difficult to constrain, and most published estimates rely on models. We analyzed size-resolved fogwater collected over two winters at Kanpur, India, by offline high-resolution aerosol mass spectrometry and apportioned by positive matrix factorization (PMF). Three highly oxidized factors (O/C 0.95–1.19) were summed as an aqSOA proxy. Combining this proxy with colocated liquid water content and water-soluble organic carbon yielded 3.1–8.4 μg m–3 aqSOA across seven events. The droplet aqSOA accounts for a median of about 7% of ambient SOA and 5% of ambient OA, reaching 13% of SOA in the densest fogs. Fine droplets carried the largest aqSOA share (43–84%), driven by higher concentrations of dissolved Fe and Cu and longer residence times. Ambient OA was less oxidized during dense than light fog (O/C 0.52 versus 0.61). Returning aqSOA after dissipation gave direct-radiative-effect increments of −0.048 W m–2 (dense) and −0.032 W m–2 (light). These size- and intensity-resolved observational constraints quantify fog–aerosol interactions and their air quality consequences in a heavily polluted region.

articles.title:
Dual-Isotope Tracing
Reveals Substantial Postanthesis
Foliar and Panicle Contributions to Grain Cadmium Accumulation in
Hydroponically Grown Rice
articles.abstract: Abstract Cadmium (Cd) accumulation in rice grains occurs through multiple exposure pathways, yet the relative contributions and associated transport mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we applied dual stable isotope labeling (112Cd/113Cd) in hydroponically grown rice under controlled conditions, with root exposure through nutrient solution as well as foliar and panicle exposure through direct solution spraying. Source apportionment was complemented by sap analysis and triple-quadrupole LA-ICP-MS imaging to examine vascular transport and allocation in the first node under the panicle (node I). Direct Cd contact with aboveground tissues inhibited growth more strongly than root exposure, inducing antioxidant responses and stomatal limitation. Isotopic mass balance revealed that under controlled hydroponic root/foliar exposure, postanthesis Cd inputs contributed 80% and 90% of grain Cd, respectively. Under triple exposure, grain Cd averaged 0.558 mg kg–1, comprising 40% foliar, 24% panicle, and 36% root contributions, demonstrating that aboveground contributions were comparable to root contributions. Transport routes diverged: root uptake elevated xylem sap Cd, whereas foliar-derived Cd showed phloem-associated localization in node I and enrichment in phloem exudates. These results highlight the role of aboveground sources in grain Cd accumulation and suggest that risk assessment in deposition-affected areas should consider both root and aboveground Cd inputs, especially during reproduction.

articles.title:
Resuspension
of
Micro- and Nanoplastics Trapped in
Coastal Sediments: Insights into Their Cross-Interface Transport and
Environmental Fate in Transitional Zones
articles.abstract: Abstract Changes in environmental conditions may drive the transfer of micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) between sediment layers and overlying waters, yet their resuspension behavior in coastal transitional waters and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study comprehensively investigated the resuspension dynamics of MNPs from sediments with different properties, as well as the effects of aquatic environmental conditions, including salinity, sediment water content, and hydrodynamics, on MNP resuspension. Sediment grain size and mineralogical composition played a dominant role in governing MNP resuspension. Differences in resuspension behavior between microplastic and nanoplastic particles were identified. MNP resuspension showed a nonlinear response to salinity, with increasing salinity generally suppressing resuspension. Resuspension was highly sensitive to salinity changes within the low-salinity range. A U-shaped pattern was observed in PSNP resuspension, with the resuspension rate initially decreasing as sediment water content declined and then increasing as sediments became drier. Positive correlations between MNP resuspension and fluid shear rate were observed, while sediment-trapped MNPs exhibited distinct sensitivities to hydrodynamic disturbances between freshwater and marine conditions. Trapped MNPs were more susceptible to hydrodynamic disturbance under freshwater conditions. These findings offer valuable insights into MNP resuspension and advance understanding of their vertical transport and overall environmental fate in coastal regions.

articles.title:
Unraveling the Differentiated
Roles of Reactive Chlorine
in Regulating Atmospheric Oxidation and Secondary Formation
articles.abstract: Abstract Reactive chlorine species significantly perturb atmospheric oxidation, yet systematic observations of multiple chlorine species and comprehensive assessments of their distinct photochemical roles remain limited. Here, we present concurrent field measurements of four reactive chlorine species (ClNO2, Cl2, HOCl, and NCl3) in a coastal urban atmosphere. Cl2 photolysis dominated Cl• production (40.2%), whereas HOCl photolysis served as a dual source of Cl• and OH•, a mechanism previously overlooked, and most effectively elevated ROx• levels. Temporally, ClNO2 photolysis enhanced early morning oxidation, Cl2 prevailed around noon, and HOCl dominated the afternoon radical budgets, while NCl3 photolysis contributed minimally throughout the diurnal cycle. Incorporating chlorine-induced volatile organic compounds (VOC) consumption in the box model amplified O3 and PAN production by up to 43.4 and 43.8%, respectively, without altering the VOC-limited regime. Our findings underscored that regulating coastal atmospheric oxidation required a species-specific, time-resolved treatment of chlorine chemistry, with direct implications for air quality management.

articles.title:
Small
Modular Electrochemical
Containers for Decarbonization
of AI Data Centers
articles.abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is increasing data-center electricity demand and reinforcing the near-term role of fossil-fuel power generation. Decarbonizing this infrastructure requires carbon capture systems that are efficient, compact, modular, and compatible with space-constrained data centers. Here, we evaluate Small Modular Electrochemical Containers (SMECs) as a deployment-oriented application of a two-stage, membraneless electrochemically mediated amine regeneration (EMAR) process. The design integrates CO2 absorption and electrochemical desorption within one gas-diffusion-electrode cell, eliminating absorber columns and ion-exchange membranes. Single-cell experiments were conducted under simulated natural-gas and coal-derived flue gas. Polarization mapping identified optimized operating conditions, which were then used in a 300-cycle, 50-h accelerated stability test with periodic polarity switching. The cell maintained repeatable voltage and CO2 absorption/desorption profiles, with absorption and desorption efficiencies of ∼90% under optimized conditions. The energetics ranged from 50–85 kJe/molCO2, and GC/IC analyses showed no detectable gaseous or liquid side products. The paper further includes theoretical modeling of SOx and NOx effects on the absorbent. In a case study for a 360 MW data-center power plant, the TEA showed that fewer than 20 SMEC units could achieve near-complete decarbonization, increasing the levelized electricity cost from about \$58/MWh to \$74/MWh.
